items.t: Fee-simple lots are the default form: The zoning base is rural: Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019's schedule lists minimum lot areas of A-1 2.0 ha, A-2 4.0 ha, A-3 8.0 ha, RS-2 0.4 ha and RS-3 0.8 ha or 2.0 ha depending on the zone text — the rural zones that cover most of this hillside. Its "89% single-detached" share is likewise not verified.

Bare-land strata: none verified — count 0: The three strata complexes below are built strata on built lots, not bare-land strata, and must never be presented as lot stock. Where a bare-land strata lot did exist, the buyer would own the lot as a strata lot: strata fees and bylaws apply to the lot itself, and the purchase runs on a Form B (SPA s.

Assemblies / plan holds — documented as plans, never as inventory: (1) Urban Reserve: the OCP's Urban Reserve designation identifies lands the City holds for long-term future urban services and housing, and OCP policy states development of the Urban Reserve will not happen until specific triggers and milestones have been attained. 10.2.2, with subdivision below 2.0 ha restricted until the city population exceeds 100,000 and an area plan is adopted — was NOT confirmed in the OCP chapter read for the research: Not verified as to hectarage, section number and trigger wording. (2) North 256 Street Industrial Lands Area Plan covers both sides of 256 Street north of 128 Avenue (about 500 acres, per the City release) at this area's north side; it establishes future designations and does not itself approve construction.
ALR vs non-ALR split: the City describes farms and nurseries in Thornhill, but ALR status is per-parcel — no split figure is published, so none is stated.

Servicing: rural properties here may be on wells and septic — wells are recorded in the provincial GWELLS database, and onsite sewerage must comply with the Sewerage System Regulation, including the 30 m setback from a well unless professional advice is obtained. blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Thornhill

items.t: Municipality: City of Maple Ridge, BC. The City describes Thornhill as a heavily forested, mainly residential area with several farms and nurseries, with a large mountain-biking and hiking trail network on 256 Street (17 trails, typically about an hour each). SnapStats lists "Thornhill" as a sub-area under Maple Ridge.

Main roads and commute: Dewdney Trunk Road and Lougheed Highway along the south side; 248, 256 and 264 Streets north–south; 100 Avenue and 112 Avenue east–west on the hillside. Commute times in minutes: Not verified.

Transit: route 748 (Thornhill / Haney Place) is a loop from Haney Place via 240 Street, McClure Drive, Jackson Road, 100 Avenue, 256 Street, 98 Avenue, 264 Street and 268 Street, weekday and Saturday trips only at wide intervals; route 701 runs east on Dewdney Trunk Road along the south side. No West Coast Express station in this sub-area.

Schools (Ministry-listed names/addresses only): Whonnock Elementary, 27471 112 Avenue; Albion Elementary, 10031 240 Street; Blue Mountain Elementary, 12453 248 Street; Samuel Robertson Technical Secondary, 10445 245 Street; Garibaldi Secondary, 24789 Dewdney Trunk Road. SD42 has no middle tier (K–7 / 8–12).

Recreation and services: the 256 Street trail network (City description in the first bullet); Kanaka Creek Regional Park at the west side; Whonnock Lake Park in Whonnock to the east. No recreation centre or library branch inside this sub-area — Maple Ridge Leisure Centre, 11925 Haney Place, and Maple Ridge Public Library, 130 – 22470 Dewdney Trunk Road, are in the Town Centre. No shopping centre inside Thornhill was verified on a City source: Not verified. Ridge Meadows Hospital, 11666 Laity Street (24/7 emergency); Urgent and Primary Care Centre, 121 – 11900 Haney Place, 7 days, 9:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Thornhill

items.t: Flood and hazards: the City's floodplain framework addresses flood risks from the Fraser River, the Alouette River system, steep creek watercourses and groundwater-related flooding. The City describes Thornhill as heavily forested; a City-documented wildfire interface map for specific Thornhill streets: Not verified. Parcel-level flood status: Not verified.

ALR block — full form (Thornhill farm/nursery ground): subdivision within the ALR requires Agricultural Land Commission approval, and ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Information Bulletin 09, s. 6; Strata Property Act, s. 239; Agricultural Land Commission Act, s. 21(1)). Residence caps: one principal residence per parcel, maximum 500 m²; a secondary suite only inside the principal residence; one additional residence capped at 90 m² on parcels of 40 ha or less and 186 m² on parcels over 40 ha. Farm class (BC Assessment) in full three-tier form: $2,500 of gross farm income at 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 plus 5% of the actual value of the area over 4 ha above that; $10,000 under 0.8 ha — applications by October 31.

Presales (REDMA) — Rydge units only: REDMA s. 21 gives a 7-day rescission period from the later of signing or acknowledging the disclosure statement, with deposits in trust under s. 18 — the frame for any unit still on a developer contract at Rydge.

The bus that serves the hillside runs at wide intervals, weekdays and Saturdays only. Route 748's Thornhill loop is not a frequent-service corridor — acreage buyers here are driving; price the lot on today's service, not on any corridor plan (the adopted Lougheed corridor ends at 221 Street, west of here).

blocks.text: Local rules that affect acreage buyers in Thornhill

items.t: Zoning: Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019: — minimum lot areas A-1 2.0 ha, A-2 4.0 ha, A-3 8.0 ha, RS-2 0.4 ha, RS-3 0.8 ha or 2.0 ha per the zone text; verify a specific parcel's exact zone with the City before pricing any use.

Suites and SSMUH: one secondary suite per lot in listed zones including A-1, A-2 and A-3, contained within the single detached building, maximum 40% of gross floor area, not in the Floodplain Area; on ALR parcels the ALR Use Regulation governs instead (suite inside the principal residence only, s.31; additional residence only under s.32). Eligible single-detached and duplex lots may have up to three, four or six units under the City's SSMUH bylaws — on rural/ALR ground the ALC frame above controls first.

If a strata purchase is made here (the three townhome complexes): Pad ground is not lot stock / land / acreage; pad tenancy percentages only (2026 = 2.3% + proportionate; 2027 = 2.2% + proportionate), NO pad-rent dollar figure as fact.
